openings.claim: Two opposed padded removable strip-pair clamps separate retention from positioning: upper strips retain separation with balanced modest preload; strip edges or bolt shafts bear against hatch edges instead of relying on seal friction. Tether hardware; park clamps outside the opening.
openings.discriminator: Hypothesis: reducing preload while retaining capture preserves position under 20 N without opposite-corner lift; the same padded compression/friction-only rival should slide more at equivalent low preload. Reopening within 30 seconds and surviving the right-contact card are also hypotheses. Compare disturbed trials at the same marked preload; differences could confound comparison.
openings.probe: First check rim underside access, strip reach, bolt length and recoverable parking. Fabricate only if supplied geometry permits reversible capture without destructive seal contact. Use only supplied equipment/materials; drill only strips. Twelve closure/pull trials: one disturbed low-preload friction-rival trial, ten candidate opening cycles with closure/pull checks, then one disturbed low-preload candidate trial. Each disturbed trial uses the 1 mm right-contact card; all requirements except seal-contact continuity remain. Record displacement, corner lift, visible seal damage and reopening time. Reject displacement over 1 mm, failure at 20 N, reopening over 30 seconds, seal tears, opening obstruction or permanent deformation. No drilling/cutting/gluing hatch or trough, powered mechanism or unrecoverable loose hardware.
openings.uncertainty: Indispensable accessible rim geometry supporting supplied strip/bolt capture and lateral bearing is unknown. Balanced preload may still rock; rubber-pad compliance and bearing capacity are unmeasured. Fast release and safe tether parking are unproven. Schedule feasibility within twenty observation minutes is undemonstrated; fabrication allowance is ninety minutes.

lineage.reason: Causal separation, complete rival prediction, disturbance comparison, rejection conditions, declared uncertain fit and resource/feasibility caveats retained.

decision: Prototype question only. Missing geometry can defeat fabrication before testing; unknown resources authorize neither constraint relaxation nor extra equipment. Success supports only this stipulated fixture.
